content.comment_body: Hello everyone, At work, I received an older [product_name] ([article_no]). It was removed from service because the customer reported that the program had been lost after the device was without power for an extended time. When powered on, the device starts in the menu with options like Program, Clock, and Start, or sometimes in the Edit menu. In both menus, the cursor keys do not respond. However, I am able to switch from the Edit menu to the Program menu by holding down the ESC key, but that's the only function currently available. Has anyone experienced similar issues with [product_name], or does anyone have suggestions for restoring its full functionality? Best regards, [user_name]

Hello everyone, I resolved the issue. The device had been in a dirty location, so after cleaning it inside—especially around the where the cursor keys make contact—it started working again. Now, the [product_name] is fully operational. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user encountered unresponsive cursor keys on an older [product_name] that had been stored in a dirty environment for a long period without power. This prevented menu navigation and limited operation to switching menus via the ESC key. Cleaning the internal contacts restored normal functionality, indicating that physical contamination can negatively impact device usability.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipated being able to use all navigation keys on the [product_name], especially to access menus and programming features.
